prosecution_argument.correct_value: Prosecution case: deceased was beaten and set on fire by the appellant and family after dowry harassment; harassment soon before death proved.
prosecution_argument.quote: the deceased told them that she was given beatings and set on fire by the appellant and his family members
prosecution_argument.reason: Prosecution's case was that she was set on fire by the accused, not that he led to suicide.

defence_argument.correct_value: Defence: no proof of dowry demand soon before death; suicide note exonerates; deceased's suicide was caused by uncle's harassment; parity with acquitted mother and brother.
defence_argument.quote: the deceased committed suicide on account of harassment by her uncle Raghubir Lal (PW-12)
defence_argument.reason: Omits the defence claim of suicide caused by the uncle; misstates the note as showing no harassment.

legal_principle_applied.quote: in the present case, there is plethora of evidence to prove the demand of dowry 'soon before the death' giving rise to the presumption against the appellant
legal_principle_applied.reason: Matches the court's application of the 'soon before death' test and the s.113B presumption.

precedent_relied_upon.correct_value: Hira Lal (2003) 8 SCC 80 relied on; Manohar Lal (AIR 2014 SC 2555) referred to and distinguished

precedent_relied_upon.reason: Manohar Lal was only referred to and distinguished, not relied upon by the court.

sentencing_rationale.correct_value: Concurrent orders on conviction and sentence were not disturbed; husband's higher responsibility to wife was the basis for rejecting parity.
sentencing_rationale.quote: we do not find any reason to interfere with the concurrent orders of the courts below in convicting and sentencing the appellant
sentencing_rationale.reason: Judgment gives no separate sentencing reasoning; the stated reasons concern conviction and parity.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: No mitigating factors are discussed by the court.

judicial_aggravating_factors.correct_value: Husband's heightened responsibility for wife's safety; prevalence of dowry deaths in society
judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: Responsibility of the husband towards his wife is qualitatively different and higher as against his other relatives.
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Court did rely on the husband's higher responsibility and the dowry-death menace, not 'None'.
